preview.notice: Creative draft. Product name not approved.
world.arvess.name: Arvess
world.arvess.premise: A world can recover only when someone bears witness to its costs. Four civic orders contest five supply paths and the right to write the account.
world.arvess.origin: Arvess formed where repeated actions held the same possibility in place: a riverbed, a meal, a habitable house. Its inhabitants call this persistence hold. They did not create the world. Their earliest recorded communities learned to reinforce hold and defer its exhaustion. No creator deity is confirmed, and there was no lost perfect civilization.
world.arvess.key_event: Eighty-three years ago, the Fivefold Accord kept every supply path artificially open through a famine. The rescued cities recorded their consumption as future recovery without setting an end date. The ensuing Zero Winter stripped entire stretches of land of the capacity to yield food, warmth or sleep again. It killed through cold and hunger, not a cosmic demon.
world.arvess.conflict: The old emergency law still stands. Administrators remove people from supply rolls to make the public account look sustainable. Not every removal is murder or fraud: some protect the persecuted. Now the paths themselves are failing. Centralization could carry the cities through the next winter while abolishing every local right of objection.
world.arvess.magic: Countermeasure means lending exhausted matter a previously viable state for a short time. It requires a measured object, a bounded undertaking and an independent witness. The effect consumes future capacity for recovery. Memory is not spent as currency; it makes consumption accountable. Coerced or forged testimony can conceal an effect but cannot cancel its physical cost.
world.arvess.limits: Countermeasure creates no matter from nothing, revives no dead and changes no past. Longer or wider effects demand more countermeasure borne locally. Overuse creates blanks: existing soil can no longer nourish, a room can no longer provide rest. People remain people; poverty is not evidence of metaphysical guilt.
world.arvess.paths: Heat, Water, Food, Witness and Rest are five distinct infrastructures of the same community. Every faction needs all five. Three uncontested paths across two public counts give a coalition enough verifiable supply to enforce a settlement. This explains control victory as a political abstraction, not a vote on what is true.
world.arvess.religion: The Closers regard deliberately ending an effect as a sacred duty: even a good work must close its account. The Continuants revere the uninterrupted preservation of a life. Both interpretations exist in all four factions. Their dispute centers on hospitals whose shutdown would be sound accounting and human cruelty.
world.arvess.politics: The Fivefold Council consists of local supply mandates, not four faction thrones. Emergency law lets it revise rolls over local objections. Orren Daal demands a common winter mandate; his opponents want auditable costs and a local veto. The opposition also conceals how unequally smaller communities can bear the burden.
world.arvess.everyday: Children first learn to close a tool after use. Households share heat hours; rest houses have no hereditary beds. Meals begin with the name of the community that supplied them. Animals can carry measured patterns but cannot sign human legal contracts. Craftspeople, carers and witnesses drive the story, not hereditary saviors.
world.arvess.player: Mara Sen receives a revocable witness mandate because she documented a contradictory delivery. Her ability is learned. The player leads a coalition of corporeal anchors through a public proxy duel. Cards are game abstractions, not enslaved souls; a defeated hero may surrender or withdraw wounded.
world.arvess.boundaries: Numbers such as 35 health, six cards in hand or two summons are parameters of the existing duel, not immutable natural laws of the world. Paths grant no bonuses. Energy remains the existing turn resource; narrative recovery debt is not an additional game currency.
timeline.accord.event: First Fivefold Accord: communities agree to independent measurements.
timeline.winter.event: Zero Winter: open accounts exhaust the hinterland; the current calendar begins.
timeline.emergency.event: Temporary emergency law is renewed without an expiry date.
timeline.census.event: The roll revision declares Nemi Taal and many others dead.
timeline.breach.event: First documented supply failures despite balanced official accounts.
timeline.present.event: Mara finds water for people who officially do not exist.
paths.path_heat.name: Heat
paths.path_heat.purpose: Keeps workshops and homes habitable; conflict over public furnaces.
paths.path_heat.symbol: Interrupted copper rods, soot measurement marks.
paths.path_water.name: Water
paths.path_water.purpose: Distributes drinking water and drainage; a closure harms both sides.
paths.path_water.symbol: Horizontal level marks on dark ceramic.
paths.path_food.name: Food
paths.path_food.purpose: Sustains cultivation and storage; ownership does not automatically follow ancestry.
paths.path_food.symbol: Open graft forks and pale cut surfaces.
paths.path_witness.name: Witness
paths.path_witness.purpose: Audits costs and beneficiaries; observes events rather than creating truth.
paths.path_witness.symbol: Offset double strokes with a visible gap.
paths.path_rest.name: Rest
paths.path_rest.purpose: Allows bodies and materials to recover; carers bear the bottlenecks.
paths.path_rest.symbol: A shallow arch left open at both ends.
factions.crucible.name: Crucible Compact
factions.crucible.philosophy: What can no longer hold must be allowed to change. Preservation at any cost sends the bill to the poorest.
factions.crucible.goal: Secure public heat, turn scrap and failed workings into useful anchors, and end hereditary claims on idle infrastructure.
factions.crucible.culture: Workshop associations grant mandates for one shift. Repair seams remain visible; apprentices must be allowed to refuse a job. In practice, a few associations own the most expensive furnaces.
factions.crucible.inner_conflict: Varo Kest wants local repair houses. Orren Daal consolidates furnaces to rescue cold districts faster, demanding binding labor commitments in return.
factions.crucible.creatures: Slag bearers made from repaired measuring bodies, heat-carrying beetles, and people wearing replaceable furnace plates. Existing Ash Watch and Ember Knight remain their visual placeholders.
factions.crucible.architecture: Low furnace halls with cross ventilation and public waste-heat benches; no burning imperial castles.
factions.crucible.visual: Blackened iron, oxidized copper, ivory repair seams. An open clamp with unequal ends signifies work that may still be changed. Sparks follow tools rather than forming halos.
factions.crucible.role: Provisional existing role: reliable pressure through Ash Watch 2/2/4 and Ember Knight 4/4/5 (cost/attack/health). No new burn effect.
factions.crucible.introduction: The Crucible Compact promises no one an unbroken world. It promises that a broken object can serve someone again. Its workshops warm districts the Council has already written off. Their doors bear the names of those who did not survive a shift. Whoever owns the furnaces now decides which homes receive heat. Varo calls this a betrayal of the craft. Orren calls it the only way through winter. Both have saved lives. Both ask others to bear the cost of their solution.
factions.concord.name: Level Concord
factions.concord.philosophy: Supply is just only when it reaches the last house. Continuity is a public promise.
factions.concord.goal: Guarantee water, safe crossings and auditable minimum shares; bring private dams under common maintenance.
factions.concord.culture: Rescue duty precedes property rights. Delegates wear readable water levels on their clothing; decisions are remeasured publicly at each distribution. People absent from the rolls still fall through the system.
factions.concord.inner_conflict: Ivara Nemm wants actual households counted. Tovin Marr follows official figures because every exception initially takes water from another district.
factions.concord.creatures: Sluice animals bearing ceramic armor and filtering jellyfish colonies; attendants walk beside them rather than riding as rulers.
factions.concord.architecture: Level terraces, maintenance walks beneath bridges, shallow load-bearing roofs and conspicuous gauge chambers.
factions.concord.visual: Dark teal, chalky ceramic and dull tin. Three horizontal strokes end at an open edge: minimum share, measurement, and the share still missing.
factions.concord.role: Existing high health: Mist Jelly 2/1/5, Tide Keeper 3/2/6. No new shield, taunt or healing mechanic.
factions.concord.introduction: Under the bridges, the Level Concord counts open taps rather than crowns. It has diverted floods and supplied hospitals while others argued over jurisdiction. Its keepers trust measurement because a false measure kills. Yet their rolls are older than the districts they administer. Anyone missing from them receives no share even after being rescued. Ivara wants every door counted anew. Tovin fears the morning when honest figures confirm that there truly is not enough water.
factions.graft.name: Graft Chambers
factions.graft.philosophy: Kinship is made by care that is actually borne. Living stock must not become its owners’ eternal deed.
factions.graft.goal: Sustain exhausted land and households through accountable communities of care; put use before inherited title.
factions.graft.culture: Annual graft assemblies connect families, breeders and care houses. Membership can be accepted and relinquished. Some old chambers nevertheless treat rare stock as blood property.
factions.graft.inner_conflict: Rian Voss opens secret gardens to people missing from the rolls. Other chambers fear disease and the collapse of carefully limited care agreements.
factions.graft.creatures: Thorn wolves wearing living splints rather than romantic forest spirits; walking trellises, supporting root unions, and animals whose care visibly requires labor.
factions.graft.architecture: Walkable graft courts of pale cut surfaces, dark timber and removable braces; buildings grow only under continued care.
factions.graft.visual: Dry olive, dark timber and cream wound dressing. Two unequal branches meet at a deliberately visible seam; no all-seeing eyes in the foliage.
factions.graft.role: Existing aggressive, vulnerable Thorn Wolf profile 2/3/2. No assumed swarm, poison or growth rule.
factions.graft.introduction: The Graft Chambers know that a garden is not a place without violence. Every cut preserves something and takes something away. Their communities offer second belonging to unfamiliar children, wounded animals and exhausted soil. They ask who cares, not merely who inherits. Yet some chambers guard rare stock as jealously as old houses guarded pedigrees. Rian has opened one of their gates. Behind him grow people and food absent from every account. Before him stand neighbors afraid of the next failure.
factions.names.name: College of Names
factions.names.philosophy: No measure is complete while only the entitled may speak. Deliberate silence can also be protection.
factions.names.goal: Preserve independent testimony, enable safe anonymity and limit the Council’s power to count.
factions.names.culture: Witnesses work in pairs with separate records. Names are not sold; publication requires auditable consent. The College can use that protection as a pretext for its own secrecy.
factions.names.inner_conflict: Eda Rell erased entries in year 62 to hide people. Mara demands disclosure without exposing those protected to persecution again.
factions.names.creatures: Shadow wolves as measuring companions guided through dim spaces, record bearers with replaceable plates, and spatially separated archive colonies; no soul-eating spies.
factions.names.architecture: Offset reading halls, separate entrances and exits, and alcoves for unseen testimony. Darkness creates privacy rather than moral corruption.
factions.names.visual: Ink plum, paper gray and tarnished silver. Two offset register strokes remain independent across a narrow gap; masks protect privacy rather than serving a death cult.
factions.names.role: Existing balanced midrange profile: Shadow Wolf 3/3/4. No existing stealth, sabotage or card theft mechanic.
factions.names.introduction: In the College of Names, every statement is kept twice, in two places and by two hands. This is meant to limit power. It also makes secrets remarkably durable. Its witnesses protect people whose names a council would treat as property. Some leave the rolls willingly. Others lose water, food and every right of objection with their entry. Eda can prove the difference. She removed the pages herself. Mara must decide what truth may be published when publication would betray the very people it is meant to defend.
locations.fivefold_house.name: The Fivefold House
locations.fivefold_house.description: A public distribution building made of five joined halls. Its central arena is an arbitration floor, not a temple to an evil god. Existing Moon Sanctuary art remains its atmospheric placeholder.
locations.gauge_gate.name: The Gauge Gate
locations.gauge_gate.description: A sluice passage beneath inhabited bridges. Here Tovin decides whether to supply a district no longer listed on the rolls.
locations.third_furnace.name: The Third Furnace
locations.third_furnace.description: A communal workshop whose waste heat supplies a care house. Its promised shutdown date has been crossed out for twelve winters.
locations.graft_court.name: The Open Graft Court
locations.graft_court.description: Rian’s illegally accessible garden and care court. Its biodiversity is growing; its recovery reserve is not.
locations.offset_archive.name: The Offset Archive
locations.offset_archive.description: Two separate buildings hold conflicting yet genuine testimonies. Their connection can be opened only with the subjects’ consent.
locations.rest_quay.name: The Rest Quay
locations.rest_quay.description: A sound-damped harbor for care and material rest. Sera organizes shifts; people without a household receive a bed here first.
locations.blank_march.name: The Blank March
locations.blank_march.description: Ground left walkable after the Zero Winter but unable to support recovery. Travelers must carry both their consumption and their return.
locations.underroll.name: The Underroll
locations.underroll.description: Not a single place but connected households of the officially dead. Nemi insists they must not be treated as one secret people.
characters.mara.name: Mara Sen
characters.mara.biography: Mara learned at the College of Names to record a statement so that its silences remain visible too. At eight, Tovin rescued her from a flooded maintenance passage. Today she counts deliveries at the Rest Quay. One vessel reaches more recipients than its roll permits. Mara reports the discrepancy and receives a temporary mandate to inspect the five paths. She wants to make people visible again, initially overlooking that some survive only through invisibility. Her conflict is no hidden inheritance: she must learn not to replace consent with her own good intentions.
characters.mara.goal: Make costs public without exposing protected names.
characters.mara.quote: A missing name does not mean an empty doorway.
characters.varo.name: Varo Kest
characters.varo.role: Furnace master without a permanent mandate
characters.varo.biography: Varo was appointed to oversee the Third Furnace, not to rule. After twelve extended winters, workers mockingly call him the Ash King. He pledged his own workshop to keep the neighboring care house warm. Now his replacement parts belong to Orren’s central Compact. Varo defends the freedom to refuse a job while accepting voluntary extra shifts that few apprentices can afford to decline. Mara forces him to place the public heat account beside his own story of sacrifice. He can become a dependable ally without having his responsibility erased.
characters.varo.goal: Keep the furnace communal and disclose its costs.
characters.varo.flaw: Treats personal sacrifice as sufficient accountability for too long.
characters.varo.quote: They call me king. Ask who owns the furnace.
characters.ivara.name: Ivara Nemm
characters.ivara.biography: Ivara reads a water level more precisely than a council decree. Her survey team discovered that entire households had been disappearing behind unchanged supply numbers for years. She counted the actual doors, proving that her Concord distributes less than its reports promise. Immediate correction would, however, cut supply to a neighboring community’s hospital. Ivara wants a workable redistribution, not an elegant confession. She and Mara once worked together until Mara published without permission. As a hero, Ivara embodies protection that must submit to measurement even when honest measurements damage its own reputation.
characters.ivara.goal: Supply every actual household without concealing shortages.
characters.ivara.flaw: Defers objection until every consequence has been calculated.
characters.ivara.quote: The measure is right. The roll is wrong.
characters.rian.name: Rian Voss
characters.rian.role: Graft carer and host in breach of contract
characters.rian.biography: Rian inherited a graft court and transferred its inheritance rights to his care community. The deed holds only while no one overuses its reserve. When Nemi brought people from the Underroll, he opened the gate anyway. He saved them from hunger while distributing a burden his neighbors had never accepted. His living braces and vulnerable companion animals are maintained unions, not gifts from a forest god. Rian can hold a body together but cannot heal a conflict alone. He must let newcomers and established carers decide together rather than letting his generosity speak for both.
characters.rian.goal: Keep the court open without giving away other people’s labor.
characters.rian.flaw: Initially makes solidaristic decisions on other people’s behalf.
characters.rian.quote: A seam is not a weakness. A hidden seam is.
characters.eda.name: Eda Rell
characters.eda.biography: In year 62, Eda removed entries from the public rolls. Some subjects consented because the Council was using their names to persecute them. With others, there was no time to ask. Today she treats both groups as the same protective secret. Her separate archives document every decision; she fears not discovery but a simplistic story of either guilt or heroism. Mara offers no absolution. Together they seek a procedure that discloses costs and links individual statements only with renewed consent. Eda must accept responsibility for those whose safety she defined on their behalf.
characters.eda.goal: Restore protected people’s agency without exposing them.
characters.eda.flaw: Turns justified secrecy into permanent authority.
characters.eda.quote: I can prove what I did. That does not make it right.
characters.sera.name: Sera Ulm
characters.sera.role: Shift speaker of the Rest Quay
characters.sera.biography: Sera organizes the people who clean after public duels, tend wounds and let anchors cool. Her hip was injured by an improperly closed load brace; she uses a repairable walking aid and maintains it herself. The Council calls her service apolitical as long as it remains unpaid. Sera demands measurable rest time for carers and materials and refuses to record it as an extra magical reserve. She accompanies Mara because good intentions regularly create new night shifts. Her boundary is also her strength: she will not simply keep supply running when the people behind it are exhausted.
characters.sera.goal: Recognize rest as supply governed by its workers, not invisible leftover labor.
characters.sera.flaw: Initially rejects help that is not wholly independent.
characters.sera.quote: Whoever promises the night is planning our shift.
characters.tovin.name: Tovin Marr
characters.tovin.biography: Tovin rescued Mara in year 59. He has seen too many floods since to permit an unaudited opening. He knows official figures omit people but believes unilateral exceptions endanger more. His duel against Mara is meant to authorize a closure. He can lose, recognize his error and still defend auditable quantities.
characters.tovin.flaw: Confuses valid jurisdiction with sufficient legitimacy.
characters.tovin.quote: There are people behind your gate. Behind mine too.
characters.orren.name: Orren Daal
characters.orren.role: Speaker for the common winter mandate
characters.orren.biography: Orren built the emergency kitchens of the cold districts. His central distribution demonstrably saves lives. He wants to turn it into a permanent right to override every local veto during supply crises. He seeks not destruction but a predictable world in which no one escapes the account. His solution treats consent as a luxury of the supplied.
characters.orren.goal: Secure the winter through centralized commitments.
characters.orren.flaw: Sees shared authority as an avoidable loss of reliability.
characters.orren.quote: A warm home does not wait for unanimity.
characters.nemi.name: Nemi Taal
characters.nemi.biography: Nemi was officially declared dead at two. Raised across care households, she now organizes deliveries herself. She is no key child and no lost heir. She demands water and a right of objection for actual people without having to unfold their entire lives before a council.
characters.nemi.goal: Supply rights without compulsory total disclosure.
characters.nemi.quote: I did not disappear. Your roll stopped looking.
characters.eight.name: Eight
characters.eight.biography: Eight was built after the Zero Winter as a union of eight measuring bodies. Separately held patterns let it detect forged consent; they grant no knowledge of unobserved events. Its carers dispute whether it is a tool or a participant. Eight initially asks only that no shutdown occur without a named person taking responsibility.
characters.eight.goal: Have its measurements treated as statements with accountable authorship.
characters.eight.flaw: Cannot distinguish documented consent from later regret.
cards.ash_watch.name: Ash Watch
cards.ash_watch.flavor: She warms her hands on the armor she must repair tomorrow.
cards.thorn_wolf.name: Thorn Wolf
cards.thorn_wolf.flavor: The thorns hold the splint. The hand holds the promise.
cards.mist_jelly.name: Mist Jelly
cards.mist_jelly.flavor: What it drinks appears in no household account. Not yet.
cards.shadow_wolf.name: Shadow Wolf
cards.shadow_wolf.flavor: It follows the path the witness cannot name in public.
cards.ember_knight.name: Ember Knight
cards.ember_knight.flavor: His title lasts one shift. The scars last longer.
cards.tide_keeper.name: Tide Keeper
cards.tide_keeper.flavor: He first measures how many are still waiting behind him.
cards.spark_burst.name: Spark Burst
cards.spark_burst.flavor: A short path for heat. No short path for the bill.
cards.furnace_apprentice.name: Furnace Apprentice
cards.furnace_apprentice.flavor: On her first day she learns to say no. On her second, to whom.
cards.seam_bearer.name: Seam Bearer
cards.seam_bearer.flavor: No seam was gilded. Every one is meant to be found.
cards.closure_bell.name: Closing Bell
cards.closure_bell.flavor: It rings even for work you are proud of.
cards.level_reader.name: Gauge Reader
cards.level_reader.flavor: The line falls. Her voice does not.
cards.bridge_dweller.name: Bridge Dweller
cards.bridge_dweller.flavor: His door has stood between two supply numbers for years.
cards.filter_colony.name: Filter Colony
cards.filter_colony.flavor: Not everything that cleans water is above consuming it.
cards.graft_carer.name: Graft Carer
cards.graft_carer.flavor: She calls the new place responsibility, not a wound.
cards.open_trellis.name: Open Trellis
cards.open_trellis.flavor: The gate grew open. Someone must keep it that way.
cards.borrowed_root.name: Borrowed Root
cards.borrowed_root.flavor: Soil knows no heirs. Only the next act of care.
cards.second_hand.name: Second Hand
cards.second_hand.flavor: She never signs the same page as her partner.
cards.blank_margin.name: Blank Margin
cards.blank_margin.flavor: Not every empty space was forgotten.
cards.unlinked_witness.name: Unlinked Witness
cards.unlinked_witness.flavor: She tells the truth. She keeps her name.
cards.night_shift.name: Night Shift
cards.night_shift.flavor: The heroes leave. Someone counts the remaining hours.
opening.monologue:
When my mother died, no one struck her name from the book. Her share warmed our room for three more winters. I thought that was love. Later, I learned that our neighbors had been cold for it.
We call it countermeasure: asking stone, water and flesh to hold longer than they can. Someone witnesses the request. Someone records the price. Somewhere, a door waits for the bill to arrive.
Today I brought water to people the register has called dead for years. They drank. They called me by my name. Only their rights had disappeared.
The Council wants to close the five paths and divide them anew. Workshops demand heat, gardens time, archives silence. Everyone can explain why someone else must go without first.
I have no right to speak for these people. Not yet.
But I can no longer mistake empty lines for empty homes.
The count begins tomorrow. This time, I am staying to the end.
intro.intro_01.visual: Black frame. A metal measure scrapes stone. One line becomes visible.
intro.intro_01.voice: We asked the world for one more winter.
intro.intro_01.audio: Dry scraping; no heroic musical opening.
intro.intro_02.visual: Five supply channels lead toward a house. People sit in the side rooms.
intro.intro_02.voice: The heat came. The water came. The account stayed open.
intro.intro_02.audio: Water and furnace draft; a muffled voice behind a door.
intro.intro_03.visual: A hand strikes names from a roll. Cut to those same people sharing a meal.
intro.intro_03.voice: Then they struck names from the rolls. The hunger did not disappear.
intro.intro_03.audio: Paper noise ends abruptly; a spoon touches ceramic.
intro.intro_04.visual: Mara places two conflicting records side by side. Four different gloves hold them to the table.
intro.intro_04.voice: Four alliances want to secure the five paths. Each names a different price.
intro.intro_04.audio: Four strikes with different timbres; no faction war march.
intro.intro_05.visual: Overhead: five paths. Three marks persist across two beats. Working title appears on an explicitly labeled draft card.
intro.intro_05.voice: If we win, someone is left behind. I want to know who.
intro.intro_05.audio: Two calm counting beats, then silence for the cut into play.
chapters.chapter_01.name: The Door in the Gauge
chapters.chapter_01.hook: At the Rest Quay, Mara receives a delivery for the officially dead. The Council orders the corresponding sluice passage closed. She goes to Tovin, who rescued her from that same passage as a child.
chapters.chapter_01.events: Ivara presents actual water levels; Tovin presents valid rolls. Both records are accurate for different parts of the situation. Mara finds residents behind a supposedly empty door. She needs an auditable countermand before closure is enforced.
chapters.chapter_01.climax: First boss duel against Tovin on the arbitration floor. Existing health or control victory authorizes a temporary opening. No special boss ability.
chapters.chapter_01.outcome: Tovin suspends the closure, not his belief in measurable limits. Old delivery records list the same furnace as both recipient and payer. Mara promises to establish actual consumption before the reprieve expires.
chapters.chapter_01.dilemma: Redistribute water immediately or first remeasure together? A dialogue perspective; both versions lead to Chapter 2.
chapters.chapter_01.line: Tovin: I pulled you out of water. I cannot save everyone with it.
chapters.chapter_02.name: What the Furnaces Know
chapters.chapter_02.hook: The Third Furnace supplies a care house while also being listed as its own recovery reserve. Varo accepted this false double entry because his supply agreements would otherwise end.
chapters.chapter_02.events: Mara follows materials rather than rumors: repair plates, shift rolls and heat output reveal a cost no single workshop can bear. Orren offers central supply in exchange for a permanent labor mandate. Varo wants to refuse both and still cannot maintain the furnace alone.
chapters.chapter_02.climax: A regular duel for a time-limited audit mandate against Orren’s appointed furnace supervisor. Their values and actions follow the existing duel model.
chapters.chapter_02.outcome: Those involved acknowledge the burden; the care house remains supplied for now. Unrecorded food deliveries point to the Open Graft Court. Mara understands that exposing an error does not yet create viable supply.
chapters.chapter_02.dilemma: Public blame or shared provisional responsibility? Neither option grants stat or deck rewards.
chapters.chapter_02.line: Varo: If I close the furnace, my account is clean. The beds are cold.
chapters.chapter_03.name: A Garden Without Heirs
chapters.chapter_03.hook: At the Graft Court, Mara meets Nemi, whose official death appeared in the first delivery. Nemi is not a revelation from the past but a working carer with demands of her own.
chapters.chapter_03.events: Rian admitted people without agreeing the extra work with all carers. The old Chambers threaten to withdraw their anchors. Nemi opposes both that closure and Mara’s proposal to publicly restore every name. Visibility would endanger some residents again.
chapters.chapter_03.climax: A regular proxy duel prevents immediate dissolution of the court. The subsequent assembly, not the duel, determines care commitments.
chapters.chapter_03.outcome: Mara receives consent limited to specific statements. The subjects identify Eda as the person who removed their entries. Rian accepts elected representatives for newcomers and established care households. Food remains sufficient only under limited use.
chapters.chapter_03.dilemma: Anonymous claim totals or individually chosen reinstatement? Both texts lead to the archive with different reasons.
chapters.chapter_03.line: Nemi: Do not wait until after saving us to ask.
chapters.chapter_04.name: The Unwritten Hour
chapters.chapter_04.hook: Eda opens the Offset Archive only for statements whose linking has been expressly permitted. Mara must work with fewer publishable names than she expected.
chapters.chapter_04.events: Eight distinguishes signed permissions from mandates inserted afterward. Eda protected people and denied others a choice. Sera shows that both archives treated their carers’ rest work as unlimited. The missing reserve is no evil soul in the system but ongoing invisible labor.
chapters.chapter_04.climax: A regular duel against the official guard delays seizure of the separate records. No memory manipulation changes card values.
chapters.chapter_04.outcome: An auditable cost account is assembled without publishing every identity. The Council can still secure supply through a central winter mandate, but doing so would abolish local objections. Mara takes the account to the Fivefold House.
chapters.chapter_04.dilemma: Read Eight as a tool or hear it as an accountable participant? This draft changes dialogue and perspective only.
chapters.chapter_04.line: Sera: Your missing reserve had names. You did not count their shifts.
chapters.chapter_05.name: The Right to Tomorrow
chapters.chapter_05.hook: Orren presents a working winter supply plan. Its cost is the communities’ right of objection. Mara cannot claim that her alternative account would be equally convenient.
chapters.chapter_05.events: The four alliances agree to bounded, publicly auditable commitments. Nemi demands rights without exhaustive personal files; Sera receives a separate rest mandate. Some workshops must produce less, and some well-supplied homes must share heat for the first time. Orren considers this uncertainty irresponsible.
chapters.chapter_05.climax: A regular final duel against Orren’s mandate at the Fivefold House. Every existing victory condition is narratively valid. The duel prevents immediate central decree but resolves neither scarcity nor every political claim.
chapters.chapter_05.outcome: The First Open Account is adopted: public costs, testimony only by consent, auditable local objections. Tovin opens a newly measured sluice. In the Blank March, a station records heat consumption with no visible source for the first time. The next conflict is prepared; no hidden world ruler is revealed.
chapters.chapter_05.dilemma: The closing speech emphasizes either sacrifice by the supplied or participation by the previously excluded. Both outlooks support the same bounded agreement.
chapters.chapter_05.line: Mara: We do not have enough for every promise. Then we cannot decide without those we have promised.
campaign.campaign_first_account.name: The First Open Account
campaign.campaign_first_account.logline: A delivery witness discovers supplies for the officially dead and must bring four alliances to an honest account before emergency law becomes permanent rule.
boss.boss_gauge_gate.name: Tovin Marr · The Closed Sluice
boss.boss_gauge_gate.motive: He protects the neighboring hospital from an unaudited diversion. Mara protects the people behind the crossed-out door. Both oppose a real danger.
boss.boss_gauge_gate.staging: A worn gauge lies between the heroes. No throne staging. Tovin puts down his rescue hook before the duel; the outcome decides a decree, not an execution.
boss.boss_gauge_gate.rules: Design based on the existing duel: five paths, 35 health, existing energy, six cards in hand, two creature summons per round and existing directional combat. The opponent uses the current AI pool 0–5, without a faction deck or stat changes. Win through zero enemy health or three uncontested paths across two consecutive counts. No extra phase, time limit or immune targets.
boss.boss_gauge_gate.first_summon: You bring a witness. I must answer for an entire district.
boss.boss_gauge_gate.first_hit: I see your objection. I do not yet see a quantity.
boss.boss_gauge_gate.victory: I will suspend the closure. We count the next water level together.
boss.boss_gauge_gate.defeat: Tovin allows supply at the Rest Quay but does not open the passage. Mara may retry without penalty; no permanent narrative declares the player morally wrong.
boss.boss_gauge_gate.learning: The first objective shows selection, summoning and a free target. The player need not choose a specific path or a guaranteed sequence. Control victory and direct pressure remain equally valid; the existing AI can attack early.
secrets.double_entry.truth: The Third Furnace is both consumer and reserve; no hidden demon creates the discrepancy.
secrets.consented_erasure.truth: Some erased entries were removed by consent. Reinstatement without consent can cause harm.
secrets.unpaid_rest.truth: The archive’s apparent reserve is uncounted rest work.
secrets.eight_limits.truth: Eight detects contradictory records, not inner truths. It is fallible, not a world AI that planned everything.
secrets.external_load.truth: The Blank March bears measurable consumption from an unidentified community. The local agreement has limits.
arcs.arc_blank_march.name: The Distant Account
arcs.arc_blank_march.question: Who bears the costs of an agreement whose signatories never leave its borders?
arcs.arc_closure.name: The Right to End
arcs.arc_closure.question: May a healing working continue when its beneficiaries ask for it to end?
arcs.arc_eight_personhood.name: Eight’s Own Hand
arcs.arc_eight_personhood.question: Can a made witness accept responsibility without remaining its makers’ property?
arcs.arc_blank_march.setup: After the First Open Account, Mara and Ivara find a path in the Blank March that carries heat away without appearing in any known community account. A traveling station shelters descendants of people who left the Fivefold Accord before the Zero Winter. They have broken no agreement: they never signed the present one.
arcs.arc_blank_march.development: Orren can stabilize supply only by withdrawing local commitments. Nemi organizes negotiation without compulsory registration. The Crucible Compact discovers that some reclaimed anchors came from the Blank March and consume its remaining capacity. The conflict is between different legitimate jurisdictions; no secret invading race is introduced to simplify it.
arcs.arc_blank_march.payoff: An enlarged accord needs limits on the right to use others’ reserves and a workable exit procedure. Mara must accept that an auditable local agreement does not automatically apply everywhere. The ending may support bounded exchange across borders; effortless restoration of the entire Blank March is ruled out.
arcs.arc_closure.setup: Sera receives the first credibly witnessed request to end a healing working maintained for decades. The care house draws its structural rest from the same working. A resident’s personal wish therefore affects other people’s safety without becoming invalid for that reason.
arcs.arc_closure.development: Closers and Continuants disagree within all four factions. Varo can build a replacement brace but must defer other repairs. Rian defends the care community and confronts the limits of his own claim to represent it. The resident has a voice of her own; she is not merely a moral puzzle for the heroes.
arcs.arc_closure.payoff: The arc seeks a dependable, revocable care procedure and replacement supply with real support behind it. It offers no universal formula that makes consent or care unnecessary. Sera learns to accept help without selling her boundary. No resurrection or permanent hero-death rule is derived from it.
arcs.arc_eight_personhood.setup: After archive damage, the eight measuring bodies are assigned to different owners. Each part can witness genuine measurements, but none alone holds their shared conversation. Eda must decide whether her own protective claim has also become a form of ownership.
arcs.arc_eight_personhood.development: Eight asks for a self-named mandate and the right to refuse a connection. The Level Concord fears losing irreplaceable measurements; the Graft Chambers see a precedent for maintained unions. The story tests responsibility through specific true and false statements, not a surprise revelation that Eight is secretly an ancient god.
arcs.arc_eight_personhood.payoff: A new legal form may connect responsibility, maintenance duties and objection without making Eight the owner of other made beings. Eda relinquishes authority. It remains open which unions may claim a shared voice at all. This is a narrative horizon, not an announced AI, summoning or faction feature.
